details: Fears of rising U.S. inflation are once again pressuring global financial and cryptocurrency markets. Prediction market Kalshi now forecasts U.S. inflation could reach 5.1% this year, while a Bank of America survey indicates 40% of fund managers view a second wave of inflation as the biggest market risk. This macroeconomic concern has heavily impacted crypto assets and related equities, with Bitcoin down approximately 5% over the last week to around $76,500 and Ethereum falling nearly 8% to about $2,100. Crypto-linked stocks have also seen declines.
title: Inflation Panic Returns: Crypto Stocks Drown in Red

details: Bitcoin traded near the $76,000 mark on Tuesday, influenced by worsening global macroeconomic conditions and significant outflows from crypto investment products. Last week alone, crypto investment products recorded $1.07 billion in net outflows, with Bitcoin funds experiencing $982 million in redemptions and Ether products $249 million, ending a six-week inflow streak. Despite these bearish trends, Japan's stronger-than-expected Q1 GDP growth and the IMF slightly raising its UK 2026 forecast provided a minor "sliver of hope" for the market.
title: Bitcoin Dips to $76K Amid Macro Woes, $982M Fund Outflows

details: Bitcoin is currently facing a key test as institutional funds, including BlackRock iShares products, are engaging in profit-taking, leading to noticeable BTC selling by ETFs since May 12. This pattern bears resemblance to previous major corrections in the cryptocurrency market. Historically, summer months have proven challenging for Bitcoin, suggesting that the coming weeks could bring elevated volatility and increased downside risk for investors.
title: Bitcoin Faces Key Test as ETFs Sell, Bear Market Ahead?

details: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting indicate that more policymakers were prepared to lay the groundwork for a potential interest rate hike. This development comes amidst persistent concerns over inflation and ongoing geopolitical risks, particularly the Iran conflict, which continue to exert pressure on global financial markets and contribute to volatility in bond yields.
title: Fed Minutes Signal Preparedness for Rate Hike
